analysis:
The PR changes only docs/threat-model.yaml. The sole changed range is head lines 1887-1893, in a mitigation list under T-043 (TB-003, watchdog rollback authority). The patch adds a mitigation entry stating that the operator rollback (`darkbloom update --rollback`) uses the same journaled rollback, update lease, predecessor verification and single-slot exact-version quarantine as the watchdog rollback. It also says rollback refuses an installed bundle that differs from the recorded release, and never rolls back one Mac of a cluster pair. The entry is marked status: implemented.

This is a documentation change with no runtime effect, so it adds no new attack surface. I examined the supplied excerpts of the TB-013 text, T-007 to T-016, T-027 to T-029, T-041, T-033 to T-037, T-042 and the start of T-043 (head lines 877-1845). Those regions are unchanged context. The head excerpt ends at line 1845, before the changed lines 1887-1893, so I could not see the surrounding T-043 text or the full patch placement. I also cannot verify that the rollback code actually implements the claimed properties (lease, predecessor verification, quarantine, bundle-mismatch refusal, cluster-pair guard).

The 'implemented' status is therefore an unverified claim about code outside the supplied evidence, not an observed regression. The claim itself is security-favorable, since it describes a rollback path with the same guards as the watchdog path. No threat assumption is invalidated.

For the integration pass: confirm that the update/rollback source in the same PR, if any, matches this documented behavior, and that the single-slot quarantine and cluster-pair refusal exist in code.
